text.tspan: 3.1 Boss Selection
Before creating characters, select which boss you will face. Put their map
and summary card on the table so that you can make more informed
decisions during character creation.
Take note of the win condition for the fight and the information on the
boss summary card. Each boss comes with unique strengths and
weaknesses, and different objectives for winning. The collaborative -
competitive slider indicates how much the boss encourages you to work
together to defeat it, and some cards are more collaboratively or
competitively themed.
3.2 Round 1: Primordial Pools
Your sculpted being begins deep within the Earth, where slumbering
magics infuse rock and clay. Deal each player 2 forms, 2 limbs, and 2
impressions. Then everyone chooses one card of each type to keep. This
forms the basis of your character.
Give the player with the first form alphabetically the first player token.
From this point on, players take turns in clockwise order moving up
through the ground, developing their sculpted being with more cards.
After each section of emergence, move the first player token around
clockwise, which changes the starting player for next round.
3.3 Round 2: Crystal Depths
Flip one of each card type face up on the table. Starting with the player
with the fist player token, each player chooses between one of the face up
cards, or may take two cards from any face down pile and select one to
keep. Replace any face up cards taken before the next player picks.
3.4 Round 3: Crystal Caves
Discard any face up cards and replace with fresh cards. Repeat the process
of round 2 starting with the new first player.
3.5 Round 4: Maze of Roots
Each player selects a card type and takes 4 cards of that type from the
draw. Each player keeps of the 4.
2.3 Cards
There are three card types you can equip in Sculpt.
Forms: Describe the shape and size of your body. Your form gives you a
significant amount of capability and opportunity for synergy. Many change
your movement speed or give defensive abilities. You may only have one
form equipped, but extra forms gained during emergence may be held and
traded.
Limbs: Things attached to your form that you can use. The majority of limbs
have activated abilities, and many have attacks. You may have any number
of limbs equipped.
Impressions: The influence of wild magic, embossed on your form are
imprints that grant you personality and power. You may have any number
of impressions equipped.
A completed sculpt character will have 6 cards, which will consist of one
form and a mix of limbs and impressions. There is no limit to the total
amount of cards you may have equipped if you gain additional cards during
combat.
There are a total of 6 rounds in emergence, some give players a choice of
card to take from a visible set, some allow you to draw from a deck or
trade, and some offer a choice of good, mixed, and bad outcomes. The
emergence board describes what to do in each round. By the end of
emergence you will have a character ready to play in battle.

3 - Emergence
2 - Your Sculpted Being
2.1 Core Statistics
There are three core stats that define your character in Sculpt: Jazz, Heft,
and Weird. They are essential for your existence, and if any become entirely
wounded, you die. Each stat can be a number between 1 and 6. You will
choose your stats during Emergence.
Jazz: Represents your manoeuvrability and coordination. It affects how
likely you are to hit and critically hit with attacks. Jazz Tokens may be spent
to climb obstacles and perform feats of acrobatics.
Heft: Represents your bulk and raw strength. It affects how much
composure you have, which enables you to take a hit without being
seriously injured. Heft Tokens may be spent to break things and overpower
your foes.
Weird: Encompasses many things, including your creativity, passion, and
magical prowess. While it does not affect any core characteristic of your
being, Weird will allow you to maximise the potential of the cards you
acquire. Spending Weird Tokens may cause abilities on cards to trigger
whenever you do so, and Weird allows you to interact with many terrain
features during Combat.
2.2 Secondary Statistics
Secondary statistics are determined by your base stats. See the combat
section for a more detailed description of the mechanics that these
statistics relate to.
Hit Value: Your hit value is determined by your Jazz. When you attack, this is
the number you need on a d12 roll to hit. Set your Jazzspinner to the right
number to see your Hit value and Crit Thresholds.
Critical Thresholds: Jazz also determines your critical thresholds. When you
attack, if you roll as high as one of your critical thresholds, you get to pick
that many critical effects in addition to dealing damage.
Composure: Taking damage depletes your composure, and when it runs out
you will suffer a wound. Your composure is equal to your Heft.
Movement Speed: This is how many hexes you move when you take a move
action. The default is 4 but equipped cards may modify this. You can adjust
the dial on your spinner to track this.

text.inkscape:label: 1- What is sculpt?
text.tspan: 1 - What is Sculpt?
1.1 Literally

tspan.tspan: Sculpt is a game of creativity and combat for 3-5 players. The objective is to
create a Sculpted being and succeed in a combative trial to emerge into the
world, the first of your kind to do so. The game consists of two phases;
Emergence, where you create your character by choosing cards that grant
you abilities and personality, then Combat, where you use your sculpted
being to fight in one of many combative and collaborative modes.

text.tspan: 1.2 Vibes

tspan.tspan: Sculpt is a game where power comes from unlikely synergy, and too much
power will get you killed. It’s a game where you are constantly balancing the
need to cooperate with the other players to defeat the boss and escape,
against your desire to have more resources left when the dust settles.
Sculpt has as few rules as we could manage, for a game ultimately about
tactical character creation and combat. This means there are situations that
can unfold which are not explicitly explained here. When these situations
arise, we recommend going with the table’s consensus on what should
happen. After the game you can look up the details of the rules in the
Appendix of the rulebook or head to the discord server for full rules

text.tspan: 1.3 Vision
Sculpt is a game made by people who like messing with the games they
play. You will find blank cards of every type in this box, to use as you wish.
Additionally, if you scan the QR code on the back of this rulebook, you will
be invited to the Sculpt discord server. Here you can share photos of your
own created cards, and monthly favourites of ours will be collated. We hope
that the game can continue to evolve with feedback and contributions from
players. If you think the game would be more fun if you tried a different
ruling, please try it and let us know how it went.
